goals.text: A coding agent extracts a bundle's claims through kmctl verbs, with base kmctl's dependencies unchanged
Claims live in one per-project store, in one validated shape that later tickets reuse
A second pass hands out only the sections whose text changed

outcomes.change: Base kmctl holds the claim models, the extraction instructions and a stdlib section cutter with change keys
outcomes.checked_by: `new:tests/test_claims_sections.py` (fixture bundle: section ids, sentence splits, code fences kept whole, correction context, deprecated concepts skipped, keys change with text, title and instructions) and `tests/test_okf_fields.py` still green

outcomes.change: A git-ignored SQLite store at `.kmctl/audit.sqlite`, with versioned schema steps
outcomes.checked_by: `new:tests/test_claims_store.py` (store at the repository root, `.kmctl/.gitignore` holds `*` and `git status --porcelain` stays empty after a write, a fresh and an older-version database both open at the newest version, two writers at once)

outcomes.change: `kmctl claims todo` hands out only new and changed sections, with the instructions
outcomes.checked_by: `new:tests/test_claims_cli.py` (first run lists every section; after submits lists none; an edited section is the only one listed and its old claims are gone; a removed concept's claims are gone; no tracked or unignored file changes after any verb) and `tests/test_help.py`

outcomes.change: `kmctl claims submit` validates an answer against the claim models and stores it
outcomes.checked_by: `new:tests/test_claims_cli.py` (a valid answer is stored; a stale key, a missing sentence verdict and a malformed answer each refuse with one stderr line naming the fix; good sections in a mixed file are kept)

outcomes.change: `kmctl claims list` shows stored claims per document and kind
outcomes.checked_by: `new:tests/test_claims_cli.py` (counts per kind, one concept's claims, `--kind` filter, `--json` shape)

outcomes.change: A decision record, the manifesto, the architecture overview and the command reference describe the claims verbs and store
outcomes.checked_by: `kmctl check`, strict OKF validation in the pre-commit hooks, and the docs tests

problems.text: Claim extraction lives only in an untracked prototype that needs langchain and a model key, so no coding agent can drive it through kmctl
Nothing stores claims per project or knows which sections changed, so every pass would read the whole bundle while the median bundle commit changes 2 of 38 concepts
No claim schema is enforced on what an agent writes, so agent claims and the later automatic extractor's claims could take different shapes
